Hi Sara —

Appreciate the checklist and the clarity on constraints. I've sketched a MAP and an evaluation sprint below that maps each hosting lane to concrete acceptance criteria and a short timeline so procurement can plan. I attached our version (redwood_map_medix_v1.pdf) and a shared doc you can edit: https://docs.google.com/document/d/1a2bRedwood-MAP-medix

Quick summary / recommendation:
- Short path (fastest time to baseline): Hosted PoC for 2 weeks. Acceptance = throughput >= 50 rps at 95th token latency < 120ms and no PHI leakage in logs (we'll sign Business Associate Addendum for HIPAA-related requirements).
- Mid path (predictable production): Dedicated pool (reserved) in us-east-1. Acceptance = sustained 500 rps 99th p50 token latency < 200ms, autoscale verified, private networking/ingress rules validated.
- Long path (maximum isolation): Private (VPC or on-prem) if legal requires full customer-controlled infra. Acceptance = private control plane + KMS keys, audit log retention policy (two years), and on-prem connectivity test pass.

Evaluation sprint (proposed):
- Week 0 (this week): finalize MAP doc and attach redlines (owner: Medix / Redwood BD).
- Week 1-2: Hosted PoC (production-like dataset subset) — load test + privacy audit. Criteria above. (owner: Redwood solutions eng + Medix devops)
- Week 3: Dedicated performance run (if procurement greenlights reserved capacity) or a black-box stress test using hosted-compatible dedicated instance (owner: Redwood infra + Medix SRE)
- Week 4: Decision meeting and procurement kickoff (legal + procurement invited).

Risks / notes:
- If Medix requires HIPAA-only isolation (Legal), we should start the Dedicated procurement path immediately — lead times for dedicated pools + legal can be 4–6 weeks.
- Latency to Denver: us-east-1 typically gives better east-coast coverage; we can measure p95 from your Denver test nodes in the Hosted PoC and validate whether us-west-2 or a dual-region routing policy is needed.

Next steps I recommend today:
1) Medix to add any legal/BAA must-haves to the shared doc.
2) We schedule a 30-min technical kickoff this week (I'll propose times).
3) Redwood to spin the Hosted PoC baseline and share test harness by EOD Tuesday.

I attached the redlined MAP and a short checklist for procurement. Let me know if you want to start the Dedicated path in parallel — we can open a reserved capacity request to shorten procurement lead time.

Best,

Rachel / team — quick technical addendum for the MAP: please see the constraints below that should be reflected in acceptance criteria and the test plan.

1) Quantization/Model profile: If Medix picks a high-throughput model (e.g., 70B), we recommend an int8 run for Dedicated to hit the throughput numbers; Hosted PoC should validate functional parity with fp16 and int8 offload. Acceptance should include model output fidelity checks (BLEU/ROUGE-like scoring on your prompt set) so we don't lose quality in quantized mode.

2) KV cache sizing: For chat flows with long context, specify expected average and max tokens — we need this to size Dedicated GPUs and predict p95 latency.

3) Network egress/costs: If the majority of traffic originates from Denver, trial both us-east-1 and us-west-2 in the Hosted PoC; if us-east-1 shows >30ms higher median network RTT, we should recommend a dual-region routing policy.

4) Procurement lead time: Dedicated farm provisioning (reserved pool) can be 3–5 weeks after SOW; Private on-prem deliveries vary. If they want a hard close before year-end, open the Dedicated request in parallel with Hosted PoC.

I'll prepare a short ops checklist (GPU profile, quantization spec, KV cache config) and drop in the shared doc by EOD.

– Karthik
